mission_01: You have implemented MAML, one of the most influential meta-learning algorithms. By learning parameters that are sensitive to task-specific changes, MAML enables rapid adaptation with just a few gradient steps. The two-loop structure — inner adaptation and outer meta-update — is the template for many subsequent meta-learning methods. You implemented sinusoidal task sampling, the standard benchmark for few-shot regression, and saw how the meta-learned initialization allows quick adaptation to new sine waves. MAML's second-order gradients (differentiating through the inner loop) are computationally expensive but crucial; first-order approximations (FOMAML) skip these and still work well in practice. This algorithm has been extended to few-shot classification (with neural networks), reinforcement learning, and beyond.
